data.description:
Hims & Hers Health 72 Hour Deadline Alert: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Reminds Investors With Losses In Excess Of $100,000 of Deadline in Class Action Lawsuit Against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. - HIMS

Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC (“KSF”) and KSF partner, the former Attorney General of Louisiana, Charles C. Foti, Jr., remind investors that they have until November 2, 2026 to file lead plaintiff applications in a securities class action lawsuit against Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (“Hims” or the “Company”) (NYSE: HIMS), if they purchased or otherwise acquired the Company’s securities between August 4, 2025 and July 29, 2026, inclusive (the “Class Period”). This action is pending in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California.

What You May Do

If you purchased securities of Hims as above and would like to discuss your legal rights and how this case might affect you and your right to recover for your economic loss, you may, without obligation or cost to you, contact KSF Managing Partner Lewis Kahn toll-free at 1-833-538-3615 or via email (lewis.kahn@ksfcounsel.com), or visit https://www.ksfcounsel.com/cases/nyse-hims/ to learn more. If you wish to serve as a lead plaintiff in this class action by overseeing lead counsel with the goal of obtaining a fair and just resolution, you must request this position by application to the Court by November 2, 2026.

About the Lawsuit

Hims & Hers Health and certain of its executives are charged with failing to disclose material information during the Class Period, violating federal securities laws.

On July 29, 2026, during market hours, the Federal Trade Commission ("FTC") announced that it had filed a lawsuit against the Company "alleging that the telehealth provider shared consumers' sensitive health information about medical conditions with third-party advertising platforms despite claiming its services maintain consumers' privacy and deceives users about its billing and cancellation practices." The FTC further alleged that the Company fails to "clearly disclose that it charges consumers for prescriptions almost immediately after they submit an intake form, despite telling consumers that they will be able to consult with a medical provider to find a treatment that is 'right for them.'"

On this news, the price of Hims & Hers Health shares fell $4.32, or 14.73%, to close at $25.00 on July 29, 2026, on unusually heavy trading volume.

The case is Velanki v. Hims & Hers Health, Inc. et al., 26-cv-09313.

About Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC

KSF, whose partners include former Louisiana Attorney General Charles C. Foti, Jr., is one of the nation's premier boutique securities litigation law firms. This past year, KSF was ranked by SCAS among the top 10 firms nationally based upon total settlement value. KSF serves a variety of clients, including public and private institutional investors, and retail investors - in seeking recoveries for investment losses emanating from corporate fraud or malfeasance by publicly traded companies. KSF has offices in New York, Delaware, California, Louisiana, Chicago, and a representative office in Luxembourg.

data.title: Fitch Cuts France's Outlook to Negative on Weaker Growth, Widening Deficit — Update
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis 




  Fitch Ratings lowered its outlook on France's credit rating to negative from stable, as the country faces economic and social pressure over its debt and growing borrowing costs. 



  Fitch said the negative outlook reflects a deterioration since its August review, and cited weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. These factors are worsening debt dynamics from an already weak starting point, Fitch added. 



  Yields on France's government bonds have also risen since the last review, Fitch said. The agency said it now forecasts interest payments will increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2028 from 2.5% of GDP in 2025. Fitch also sees France's deficit at 5.5% of GDP in 2027, which it said reflects a weaker growth assessment and the risk of concessions during the budget process. 



  The next scheduled review date for France's rating hasn't yet been set, Fitch said, but added it expects to review the rating by end-February 2027 at the latest. 



  France's public debt is closing on 120% of its GDP, and the nation's economy shrank in the third quarter. The government is expecting the deficit to hit 5.4% of GDP this year. 



  In recent weeks, hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Paris and other French cities, with some protesters resorting to vandalism and violence. 



  Right-wing presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has recently cast herself as a unifying figure, and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to cancel hundreds of billions of euros in French national debt, The Wall Street Journal reported. 



  Last week, Moody's Ratings kept its Aa3 credit rating on France unchanged, citing the country's diversified economy and strong public institutions. However, Moody's retained its negative outlook on the country as France continues to face political instability and protests. 



  Moody's retains a higher rating than peers Fitch and S&P Global Ratings. S&P had lowered France's rating to A+ in October of last year. 



  Fitch affirmed the country's A+ rating, which it said is supported by a large, wealthy and diversified economy, strong institutions, euro area membership and a resilient banking sector.

  (END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.description:
Five California Nonprofits Receive $500,000 to Restore Habitats, Expand Environmental Education and Strengthen Local Food Systems

Five California Nonprofits Receive $500,000 to Restore Habitats, Expand Environmental Education and Strengthen Local Food Systems

PR Newswire

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026

Final round of PG&E Corporation Foundation grants completes a five-year, $2.5 million investment in 25 community organizations

Link to the B-roll and soundbite from Sacramento Splash

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PG&E Corporation Foundation (PG&E Foundation) is awarding five community-based organizations in Northern and Central California a total of $500,000 in grants for local initiatives dedicated to environmental stewardship.

The 2026 grant recipients represent the program's final group, completing the PG&E Foundation's five-year investment in projects that help strengthen local ecosystems and communities.

Since its launch in 2022, the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program has invested $2.5 million in 25 organizations across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PG&E) service area, advancing environmental stewardship and supporting community-led innovation.

The five organizations will each receive $100,000 through the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant program for leading efforts to preserve California's unique biodiversity, focusing on land, air quality and water stewardship.

Funding for this initiative comes from PG&E shareholders, not customers.

"For 27 years, Sacramento Splash has helped kids connect with the natural world through hands-on science and environmental education. Thanks to PG&E's support, about 7,000 students will experience Project Agriculture, Water, Energy & Environment during the 2026–27 school year, learning where their food comes from and how everyday choices can help create a more sustainable future," said Mackenzie Wieser, Chief Executive Officer, Sacramento Splash.

"We extend our sincere gratitude to all the organizations, partners and community leaders who helped make this program a success. What inspires us most is seeing local organizations turn their deep understanding of their communities into meaningful action, creating lasting impact where it matters most," said Carla Peterman, President, PG&E Corporation, and Chair of The PG&E Corporation Foundation Board.

Grant recipients are based in each of PG&E's five regions: North Coast; North Valley and Sierra; Bay Area; South Bay and Central Coast; and Central Valley. Receiving grants are:

  • Noyo Center: Kelp Forest Recovery (Fort Bragg) - Noyo Center restores Mendocino Coast kelp forests by removing invasive urchins and planting bull kelp. The project also supports red abalone recovery and environmental education. These efforts help create healthier, more resilient coastal ecosystems.
  • Sacramento Splash (Sacramento) - Project Agriculture, Water, Energy & Environment gives students in grades 2-5 from underserved Sacramento County schools hands-on learning experiences at the Historic Nicolaus Dairy in Elk Grove, often providing their first opportunity to visit a working farm. Students explore agriculture and environmental stewardship by planting and harvesting crops, building compost, observing bees, and learning about water conservation. Grant funding will support educators, transportation for Title I schools, and educational materials, helping the program reach approximately 7,000 students from 231 classes during the 2026-27 school year.
  • Friends of Sausal Creek (Oakland) - Friends of Sausal Creek will expand its paid youth stewardship program to provide year-round green job skills training for Oakland youth while helping restore the 2,600-acre Sausal Creek watershed. Participants will gain hands-on experience through habitat restoration, water quality improvements, and kayak-based estuary cleanups. In Jingletown, youth will also design and install a native planting plan and help create a community interpretive sign.
  • Point Blue Conservation Science (Bolinas) - Point Blue Conservation Science's program gives K-12 students hands-on experience restoring natural habitats while learning about environmental stewardship. In San Benito County, students, community college interns, residents, and land stewards will work with local partners to plant native vegetation and restore streamside habitat along an important wildlife corridor. The project will improve water quality, wildlife habitat, and climate resilience while providing students with education, job training and career development opportunities in conservation.
  • Black Urban Farmers Association (Stockton) – Black Urban Farmers Association (BUFA) has operated a pesticide-free urban farm in Stockton since 2015, providing fresh food and promoting regenerative farming. The project will help BUFA expand to a permanent one-acre site with more green space, education, and sustainable agriculture opportunities. Grant funding will support site planning, environmental reviews, infrastructure, and a community launch, strengthening long-term food security and environmental stewardship.

With the selection of the 2026 grantees, the application period has closed and the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program is no longer accepting applications.

About PG&E
Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE:PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit pge.com and pge.com/news.

About The PG&E Corporation Foundation
The PG&E Corporation Foundation is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, separate from PG&E and sponsored by PG&E Corporation.

data.title: Revolve Enters into Definitive Agreement to Acquire Three Project, 6 MW Battery Storage Portfolio in Ontario
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Revolve Renewable Power Corp. (CSE:REVV)(OTCQB:REVVF) ("Revolve" or the "Company"), a North American owner, operator and developer of power generation and digital infrastructure projects, is pleased to announce that, through a subsidiary, it has entered into a definitive agreement for the acquisition (the "Acquisition") of all of the issued and outstanding shares in the capital of Logan Energy Storage ULC ("Logan"). Logan owns a portfolio of three battery energy storage system ("BESS") projects located in Ontario (the "Portfolio"), with a total capacity of 6 megawatts ("MW") / 11.7 MWh. The total purchase price for the Portfolio is CAD$1,500,000 and will be funded by cash on the Company's balance sheet. The seller of the Logan is arm's length to Revolve.

The Company executed definitive equity purchase and related agreements October 30, 2026, providing for the Acquisition, which remains subject to customary closing conditions and applicable approvals. Upon closing, the Acquisition is expected to increase Revolve's battery storage capacity in Ontario to approximately 20.2 MW / 36.0 MWh across nine projects. It builds on the Company's acquisition of the six-project, 14.2 MW / 24.3 MWh Trillium Storage portfolio, completed in August 2026.

"The Logan acquisition is another important step for Revolve as we continue to build our storage platform in Ontario," said Myke Clark, CEO. "Following the completion of Trillium, this transaction is expected to increase our battery storage capacity in the province and further establish our presence in Ontario. We look forward to closing the transaction and building on this platform as we continue to execute our disciplined acquisition and development strategy."

The transaction reflects Revolve's continued strategy of acquiring assets alongside its greenfield development pipeline.

For further information contact:

Myke Clark, CEO
IR@revolve-renewablepower.com
778-946-0072

About Revolve

Revolve was formed in 2012 to capitalize on the growing global demand for renewable power. Revolve develops utility-scale wind, solar, hydro and battery storage projects in the US, Canada and Mexico. Revolve also installs and operates sub 20 megawatt ("MW") "behind the meter" distributed generation (or "DG") assets. Revolve's portfolio includes the following:

  • Operating Assets: 36.2 MW (net) of operating assets under long-term power purchase and services agreements across the US, Canada and Mexico covering wind, solar, battery storage and hydro generation;
  • Development: a diverse portfolio of utility scale development projects across the US, Canada and Mexico with a combined capacity of over 3,000MWs as well as a 140MW+ distributed generation portfolio that is under development.

Revolve has an accomplished management team with a demonstrated track record of taking projects from "greenfield" through to "ready to build" status and successfully concluding project sales to large operators of utility-scale renewable energy projects. To-date, Revolve has developed and sold over 1,550MW of projects.

data.title: Prospect Ridge Announces Closing of Critical Metals Flow-through Unit Private Placement
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. (the "Company" or "Prospect Ridge") (CSE:PRR)(OTCQB:PRRSF)(FRA:0ED) is pleased to announce that it has closed the third and final tranche of its non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") of $0.075 critical mineral flow-through units (the "FT Units") first announced on October 2, 2026, and updated on October 13th, 19th and 21st, 2026 (see news releases for details), issuing an aggregate of 2,016,669 FT Units for gross proceeds of $151,250.18. All securities issued in the third tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring on March 1, 2027.

Each FT Unit was comprised of one flow-through common share (a "Common Share") in the capital of the Company and one-half of one Common Share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase one common share at a price of $0.10 for a period of two years after closing, subject to accelerated expiry if the Company's common shares trade or close on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "Exchange") at $0.21or more for ten consecutive trading days.

In connection with the third tranche, the Company paid aggregate finder fees of $8,487.51 in cash and issued an aggregate of 113,167 finder warrants having the same terms as the warrants comprised in the FT Units (exercisable at $0.10 for two years subject to acceleration on the occurrence of certain events). There was no insider participation in the third tranche.

Over the three tranches, the Company raised aggregate gross proceeds of $1,836,375 through the issue of 24,485,004 FT Units, representing an oversubscription of $336,375 over the originally planned Offering of $1,500,000.

Over the three tranches, insiders purchased an aggregate of 335,000 FT Units, which as of the third tranche closing represented less than 1% of the then issued and outstanding shares, and less than 1% if the associated warrants were immediately exercised. The participation by insiders constitutes a "related party transaction" within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company has relied upon the exemption from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements pursuant to sections 5.5(a), (b) and (c), and sections 5.7(1)(a) and (b), respectively, of MI 61-101.

Use of Proceeds of the Offering

The Company intends to use the gross proceeds from the FT Shares to incur, on its mineral projects in British Columbia, eligible "Canadian exploration expenses" that will also qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" under the Income Tax Act. The Company intends the bulk of the gross proceeds to finance an upcoming 2,500-meter drill program on the Issuer's Camelot project, located near Horsefly, B.C. (see News Releases dated January 23, February 25 and June 16, 2026) and for preparations for an extensive Spring drill program at the Company's Excalibur project located north of Smithers, B.C (see News Releases dated September 10 and 24, 2026).

The securities to be offered under the Offering have not been, and will not be, registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act") or any U.S. state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, United States persons absent registration or any applicable exemption from the registration requirements of the U.S. Securities Act and applicable U.S. state securities laws. This news release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy securities in the United States, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

About Prospect Ridge Resources Corp.

Prospect Ridge Resources Corp. is a British Columbia-based exploration and development company focused on critical metals and gold. Led by a seasoned management and technical team with over 100 years of combined mineral exploration experience, Prospect Ridge is advancing its north-central B.C. located Golden Horseshoe and Cariboo projects - high-potential copper-gold systems positioned within one of Canada's most under-explored yet geologically endowed mineral belts.
